rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for finishing a task, piece of work, or activity.

example.english: I finally managed to complete my homework.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zung1 jyu1 zou6 jyun4 fan6 gung1 fo3 laa3

rows.note: Use this for completing a task, goal, project, or other clearly defined undertaking, especially in more polished wording.

example.english: Our team will complete this project.
example.traditional: 我哋團隊會完成呢個項目。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 tyun4 deoi6 wui5 jyun4 sing4 ni1 go3 hong6 muk6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when all the parts are present and nothing is missing.

example.english: This set of tableware is complete.
example.jyutping: ni1 tou3 caan1 geoi6 ji5 ging1 cai4 saai3

rows.note: Use this when something has reached the end and is finished or done.

example.english: My homework is not complete yet.
example.jyutping: ngo5 fan6 gung1 fo3 zung6 mei6 jyun4

rows.note: Use this before a noun or adjective when complete is an emphatic intensifier, as in “a complete bastard.”

example.traditional: 佢真係十足一個大懶蟲。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zan1 hai6 sap6 zuk1 jat1 go3 daai6 laan5 cung4

rows.note: Use this when the focus is making something whole or complete rather than simply finishing it.

example.english: Adding this page will make the book complete.
example.traditional: 補返呢一頁，就令本書完整喇。
example.jyutping: bou2 faan1 ni1 jat1 jip6 zau6 ling6 bun2 syu1 jyun4 zing2 laa3
